subject: VPC storage residency and deletion commitments for Zephyr Health (follow-up)
messages:
From: Kate Jenkins <kate.jenkins@zephyrhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: legal@zephyrhealth.com
Date: 2028-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Residency and deletion process for VPC deployment

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move ahead with the PO, our security and compliance team has a few concrete questions about the Private/VPC deployment model and how Redwood guarantees residency and deletion: 

1) Residency guarantee: Can you confirm that customer data (raw input, embeddings, snapshots) will never leave the US region(s) we select? Are there any control-plane or logging artefacts that might be replicated elsewhere?

2) Backups & snapshots: If we enable automated snapshots, where are they stored (our cloud account vs Redwood-managed storage)? Can we opt out entirely and still meet your support expectations?

3) Deletion timeline & proof: If Zephyr exercises its deletion right, what is the end-to-end timeline (including snapshots, backups, logs)? Do you provide a signed attestation or certificate of deletion?

4) Key management & encryption: Can customer keys be used (KMS/HSM)? If keys are rotated or rekeyed during handback, what is the impact on proofs of deletion?

5) Contract language: Can you share sample contract wording we can drop into our vendor agreement for residency and verified deletion?

Attached is a short spreadsheet with a few items we track (Zephyr-questions.xlsx). Please loop in folks on your side who handle operations/attestations.

Best,
Kate Jenkins
Head of Information Security
Zephyr Health

[attachment: Zephyr-questions.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kate Jenkins <kate.jenkins@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-11T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and deletion process for VPC deployment

Hi Kate — great questions, and thanks for the clear list. High-level answers first, then Marissa will add technical detail and Ben will cover contractual artifacts.

- Residency: For Private deployments we mount customer-controlled volumes in the customer VPC (you pick region/az). Customer data does not traverse Redwood-managed regional storage by default. Control-plane metadata (service orchestration events) are minimal and can be restricted to our control plane region per contract.

- Backups: Options are (a) snapshots stored in your cloud account (recommended), (b) snapshots pushed to Redwood-managed isolated buckets in the same region (only by exception). You can opt out of automated snapshots — we recommend a documented runbook if you do.

- Deletion & proof: Standard flow is tombstone -> crypto-sanitize -> physical deletion of volumes and snapshots. We typically provide a deletion attestation in the form of a signed statement and an ops timeline.

- Keys: Customer-managed KMS is supported for data-at-rest. If you use your KMS, Redwood cannot access plaintext without an explicit key grant. Rekeying is supported; we provide guidance to ensure attestations remain valid.

I attached our short Deletion Playbook and a handback checklist to help answer the PO/legal questions. Marissa — can you confirm timelines for snapshot deletion and what we can include in a signed attestation? Ben — can you share template contract wording?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kate Jenkins <kate.jenkins@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-13T11:13:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and deletion process for VPC deployment

Hi Kate — copying the relevant detail below and attaching an operational checklist. Short answers to your follow-ups: 

1) Snapshot deletion ownership: If snapshots are stored in your cloud account (recommended), Redwood will provide exact disposal commands and can run them as an ops activity if you authorize us via an IAM role/grant. If they are in a Redwood-managed bucket, we run the deletion and include those artifacts in the attestation.

2) Replication & DR copies: For Private/VPC we do not replicate data to other regions by default. Any DR replication is only enabled with explicit customer consent. We will include a no-cross-region-replication clause in the PO unless you request DR.

3) Logs & telemetry: Control-plane operational logs are retained for 90 days by default. For exit events we support an accelerated purge where we truncate control-plane logs related to tenant identifiers within 30 days; some system-level traces (generic orchestration metadata) may persist longer for platform integrity but are not tenant-data.

4) Deletion timeline & attestation: Proposed operational SLA for Zephyr: 
   - Initiation: immediate on receipt of approved deletion request.
   - Physical deletion: completed within 20 days for customer volumes/snapshots when we operate deletion; 30 days maximum if coordination with customer cloud account is required.
   - Attestation: signed attestation delivered within 10 calendar days of completion.

5) KMS: Customer-managed KMS is supported (AWS KMS, Google CMEK, Azure Key Vault). If customer KMS is used and keys are revoked after deletion, we will indicate that in the attestation to avoid ambiguity.

I've attached our \"residency-handback-checklist.xlsx\" which lists the exact artifacts we produce for attestations (deleted snapshot IDs, S3/GCS bucket names, IAM role ARNs used, ops runbook IDs).

Next steps: If Zephyr agrees to the above timeboxes we'll draft a short SLA appendix and sample contract paragraph.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Residency and deletion process for VPC deployment — proposed clause + next steps

Hi Kate / Zephyr Legal — thanks for the detailed questions. Per Marissa's notes above, Redwood can commit to the following clause language in our Master Services Agreement: 

"Data Residency & Deletion. Redwood will ensure that Customer Data stored in a Private/VPC deployment is stored only within the geographic region(s) specified by Customer. Redwood will not replicate Customer Data to regions outside the specified region(s) without Customer's prior written consent. Upon Customer's written request to delete Customer Data, Redwood will execute the agreed deletion procedure (tombstone, crypto-sanitize, delete physical volumes and snapshots) and will provide a signed attestation listing deleted artifacts and the deletion timeline. Physical deletion will be completed within thirty (30) days, and a signed attestation will be delivered within ten (10) days of completion, subject to Customer cooperation for artifacts held in Customer-managed cloud accounts."

I've uploaded a short redline of the MSA appendix for your counsel to review: https://hubspot.com/companies/ZephyrHealth/deal/ZEY-1421 (redline attached to the deal record). If that language looks acceptable, can we schedule a 30-minute legal call tomorrow to finalize the appendix and confirm the IAM role for snapshot actions?

Proposed times: 2028-04-15 09:00-10:00 PT or 2028-04-15 15:00-16:00 PT.

Thanks — happy to walk through the attestation artifacts in the call.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
